covenants.detail: Minimum Fixed Charge Coverage Ratio of 1.10x, tested quarterly on a trailing twelve month basis.
covenants.clause: Section 6.01(a) of the Credit Agreement: Borrower shall maintain a Fixed Charge Coverage Ratio of not less than 1.10 to 1.00, tested as of the last day of each fiscal quarter for the four quarters then ended.
covenants.notes: Fixed charges are scheduled principal and interest on all funded debt, cash taxes, unfinanced capital expenditure, ESOP contributions and distributions. Q2 2026 test at 1.24x. The ratio is tightest in Q1 when the ESOP contribution falls.

evaluations.comments: Q4 2025 test at 1.33x, the first test after the ESOP closing. Compliant.
Q1 2026 test at 1.13x, the tightest quarter of the year once the ESOP contribution and the annual insurance renewal are counted as fixed charges.
Q2 2026 test at 1.24x, recovered with the spring restocking margin.
Q3 2026 test period open. Certificate due 30 October 2026.

covenants.detail: Minimum availability block of $1,500,000 under the asset based revolving line, tested on each monthly borrowing base certificate.
covenants.clause: Section 2.06 of the Credit Agreement and Schedule 2.06 (Availability Block): Borrower shall at no time permit Availability to be less than $1,500,000.
covenants.notes: Availability is the lesser of the commitment and the borrowing base, less advances and less the standby letter of credit exposure. The last recorded covenant evaluation is the April 2026 certificate, which reported availability of $1.18MM against the $1.50MM block after a seasonal inventory build and a slow April collection cycle. The block cured on the May 2026 certificate at $3.9MM once the build sold through, and availability was $5.25MM at 31 July 2026. Policy exception CI-AVL-01 records the April breach and remains unmitigated in the file. The next formal test is the September 2026 certificate.

evaluations.comments: February 2026 certificate. Availability $2.64MM, inside the block but tightening on the spring inventory build.

April 2026 certificate. Availability $1.18MM against the $1.50MM block. Caused by a $2.1MM inventory build ahead of the Midwest Dental Conference and a nine day slip in the collection cycle. Policy exception CI-AVL-01 raised, unmitigated.
May 2026 certificate. Availability $3.90MM. The block cured without any change to structure or advance rate.
July 2026 certificate. Availability $5.25MM on a $16.92MM base against a $15.00MM commitment.

covenants.detail: Springing global debt service coverage of 1.00x, tested only while availability is below $2,250,000 and for the two consecutive testing periods that follow.
covenants.clause: Section 6.01(b) of the Credit Agreement: if at any time Availability is less than $2,250,000, Borrower shall maintain a Global Debt Service Coverage Ratio of not less than 1.00 to 1.00, tested for the trailing twelve months as of the most recent month end and on each subsequent test date until Availability has exceeded $2,250,000 for two consecutive months.
covenants.notes: Global coverage consolidates the borrower, Lakeshore Logistics LLC and the personal debt service of both guarantors. The covenant sprang on the April 2026 certificate when availability fell to $1.18MM and was tested at 1.06x, inside the 1.00x floor. Availability has been above the $2.25MM trigger every month since May 2026, so the covenant is dormant again. The September 2026 date is the standby test that would apply if the trigger were hit again.

evaluations.comments: Sprung by the April 2026 availability breach. Global coverage tested at 1.06x on a trailing twelve month basis, inside the 1.00x floor.
Second consecutive test after the spring. 1.11x. Availability back above the $2.25MM trigger, so the covenant fell dormant after this test.

covenants.detail: Semi-annual field examination of accounts receivable and inventory by the bank or its agent. Verified variance against the reported borrowing base may not exceed 5 percent.
covenants.clause: Section 5.09 of the Credit Agreement: Borrower shall permit not fewer than two field examinations in each calendar year, at Borrower expense, and shall grant the examiner access to all books, records and locations.
covenants.notes: OVERDUE. The February 2026 examination reported a 2.4 percent variance against the certificate and no dilution finding worth a reserve. The August 2026 examination was due on 14 August and has not been performed: the examiner rescheduled twice around the borrower's inventory count and the bank has not re-booked it. Policy exception CI-FEX-02 waives the timing to 31 October 2026.

reviews.narrative: FY2025 annual credit review of the Lakeshore relationship, the first full review since the November 2025 ESOP transaction. Grade affirmed at 5.
reviews.summary: Lakeshore group: $29.95MM committed across nine booked facilities in three packages, $23.475MM outstanding. The asset based package carries a $15.0MM revolver on an 80 and 50 borrowing base with a $1.5MM availability block, a $3.5MM ESOP term loan and a $900K equipment note. The real estate package carries the $5.9MM first mortgage and a $450K improvement note on the Glendale distribution centre, borrowed by Lakeshore Logistics LLC. The growth package carries the Madison branch term loan, the vehicle note, the racking note and a $300K standby letter of credit facility. Secured by a first blanket lien on receivables, inventory, equipment and titled vehicles, and by first and second mortgages on the distribution centre. Guaranteed without limit by both founders on the operating facilities and with capped guaranties on the real estate.
reviews.recommendation: Renew the $15.0MM revolving line at WSJ Prime plus 0.50 percent for a further twenty four months at the November 2027 maturity. Hold the grade at 5. Complete the overdue August field examination before 31 October 2026 and report the findings to credit before the renewal is documented.
reviews.riskComments: Risk grade affirmed at 5. Fixed charge coverage of 1.24x at Q2 2026 is inside the 1.10x covenant with the tightest quarter, Q1, at 1.13x. Senior leverage rose with the ESOP debt and is amortising on schedule. The April 2026 availability breach is the only covenant miss and it cured without a change to structure or advance rate. The overdue field examination is a bank process failure rather than a borrower failure and is the main open item on the file.
reviews.strengths: Thirty eight year operating history under the founding management, both of whom remain in day to day control after the ESOP sale. Recurring consumables revenue with 4,100 practice customers and no customer above 3 percent of sales. Owner occupied real estate with $1.85MM of equity above the two mortgages. Inventory turns of 6.1 and a dilution rate of 1.9 percent verified at the February field examination.
reviews.weaknesses: Seasonal working capital swing around the spring conference and restocking cycle, which is what pushed availability through the block in April 2026. Leveraged ESOP debt service is a permanent new fixed charge that takes Q1 coverage close to the covenant. Margin pressure from group purchasing organisations on consumables. The August 2026 field examination is overdue and the borrowing base has not been independently verified since February.

reviews.narrative: First half 2026 covenant review for the Lakeshore asset based package, covering the four covenants in the credit agreement.
reviews.summary: Four covenants tested in the first half of 2026: fixed charge coverage at 1.13x in Q1 and 1.24x in Q2 against a 1.10x minimum, both compliant; the $1.5MM availability block breached in April at $1.18MM and cured in May at $3.9MM; the springing global debt service coverage tested at 1.06x and 1.11x when the April breach sprang it, both inside the 1.00x floor; the semi-annual field examination performed in February with a 2.4 percent variance and overdue since 14 August 2026.
reviews.recommendation: No structural change. Book the field examination for October and confirm the borrowing base ineligible categories with the controller before the examiner attends. Keep policy exception CI-AVL-01 open until the September and October certificates confirm availability above the block through the autumn restocking cycle.
reviews.riskComments: One covenant breach and one overdue reporting covenant in the period. Neither is grade changing. The availability breach was seasonal and self curing; the overdue examination is a scheduling failure on the bank side.
reviews.strengths: The borrower produced every monthly certificate on time, including the April certificate that reported its own breach.
reviews.weaknesses: Availability has no cushion in the April and May window without either a lower inventory build or a temporary overadvance.

riskRatingReviews.comments: Annual risk rating review supporting the FY2025 annual review. Computed grade 5. The model output was affirmed without override: the ESOP leverage is offset by the recurring consumables revenue base and the verified collateral coverage.
